records.quote:
He felt the refinished wall, his fingertips searching for hidden
panels. There was none.
records.paraphrase: Ernie physically investigates the wall to find a hidden explanation for the vanishing door.

records.quote:
"Oh, you and I have lived in the same vicinity all our lives,
even crossed each other's paths, but we are in different
dimensions--different worlds in the same place."
records.paraphrase: The host describes overlapping dimensions occupying the same space with parallel people.

records.quote:
"Kronkite,
Ernie here says we are thirty degrees off. Can you shift the
equilibrium?
records.paraphrase: A technician is asked to adjust the equilibrium of the dimension to correct its tilt.

records.quote:
It was as if the
wall were twelve inches thick--as if
he were not hearing anything at all--and yet hearing.
records.paraphrase: Ernie hears voices that seem to come from behind a wall where nothing should be.

records.quote:
He was not a man of hallucinations. He was
not a victim of superstition, fear or near-sightedness. He only wanted
to know why he saw a door one day and didn't see it the next.
records.paraphrase: Ernie asserts his rationality and seeks a logical reason for the door's inconsistent appearance.

records.quote:
we will install a series of
transitional burnouts. These will break down molecular resistance which
our more powerful equipment creates on solid portions of your house.
records.paraphrase: The host describes using transitional burnouts to break down molecular resistance to align the dimension with the house.

records.quote:
For when the other you enters our hallway
door, we shall have to do away with one of you.
records.paraphrase: The duplication error means one of the two Ernies must be eliminated.

records.quote:
For Ernie Lane had stopped walking
hurriedly past that extra door, had stopped giving it only casual
curiosity, had even stopped wondering afterward.
records.paraphrase: An extra door in the house appears and disappears, prompting Ernie's growing attention.

records.quote:
walked to a little white
building near the Washingable Monument, stepped inside, handed a man
his Other World card, then walked through a door, felt sick at his
stomach, came out to the streetcar line to Melinee and home.
records.paraphrase: Ernie uses a pass to travel through a door between dimensions back to his own world and home.

records.quote:
The pale green wall of the hallway confronted him. It was as if the
door were merely hinged onto the wall. No opening whatever.
records.paraphrase: The extra door opens onto solid wall with no opening behind it.

records.quote:
It turned his mind, his body, wrong-side out. Like the
squeezing out of a wet mop by a steamroller.
records.paraphrase: Passing through the opening physically distorts Ernie as he crosses into the other space.

records.quote:
slung bottle after
bottle at the instruments, caused three small explosions, a sputtering
red fire, a terrible burst of black smoke and a sudden explosion that
turned the whole new dimension--such as it was--into a white blinding
sun.
records.paraphrase: Ernie destroys the experimental equipment, causing explosions that obliterate the new dimension.

records.quote:
there was a technical miscalculation in our instruments
which, while allowing you to enter this new dimension, also did not
allow you to enter.
records.paraphrase: A miscalculation produced a paradox in which Ernie both entered and did not enter the dimension.

records.quote:
The
whole thing seemed to be about thirty degrees lopsided.
records.paraphrase: The hidden room's floor is tilted about thirty degrees.

records.quote: "There was an explosion in the night. I think it was gas escaping."
records.paraphrase: Ernie explains the night's events to his wife as an ordinary gas explosion.

records.quote:
What we are
both in is a third realm sponsored by the government--the federal
government of The Unison States. Congrice sponsored this scientific
investigation
records.paraphrase: The setting is an experimental third dimension funded by a parallel-world government's scientific program.

records.quote:
Melinee? It was all like a breath of spring. Away from that house, she
was a different person.
records.paraphrase: The narration contrasts the wife's identity away from the house versus inside it.

records.quote:
"This is your house, of course, but we're not quite there yet. We're in
what you would call--oh, another dimension."
records.paraphrase: Ernie's host explains they are in another dimension coincident with his house.

records.quote:
The dimensions immediately struck Ernie as all wrong. It was far bigger
than the hall closet where it was supposed to be.
records.paraphrase: The concealed space is impossibly larger than the physical closet that should contain it.

records.quote:
"Our object, of course, is to start out the new dimension with an Adam
and Eve," the host said.
records.paraphrase: The experiment's goal is to populate a new dimension starting with Ernie and Marsha as founders.

records.quote:
"Darling, don't call me
Melinee when my name is Marsha. It just isn't done."
records.paraphrase: Ernie's wife shifts between being Melinee (blonde) and Marsha (red-haired), a change tied to the house.

quarantined.reason: quote could not be located in prepared story

candidate.quote:
"Melinee in your dimension, Marsha in ours. You and she exist in our
dimension as well. Same types, same characteristics inwardly. But not
the same outwardly."
candidate.paraphrase: The host explains that people exist in both dimensions with the same inner nature but different outward forms.

candidate.quote:
"The extra door in the hallways? Sooner or later she
will see it, wonder as you did and open it. This time we will have the
magnetic field force turned on.
candidate.paraphrase: The door is a magnetic field-force entrance intended to pull people into the dimension.

candidate.paraphrase: A duplicate of Ernie, named Irvin, arrives at the door, realizing the feared doubling.

criteria.rationale: The story materially invokes the speculative science of parallel dimensions occupying the same space, a government-sponsored scientific investigation into extra-dimensional realms.

An engineered dimensional apparatus (equilibrium shifter, transitional burnouts, magnetic field-force door, Congrice-rigged contraption) materially drives the setting, the trapping problem, and the climax when Ernie destroys it.
The displacement is spatial/dimensional rather than temporal; no future era, remote past, or time travel is materially present.
Consequences are developed from the dimensional-experiment premise: the plan to found a new world with an Adam-and-Eve pair, and the miscalculation producing a duplicate Ernie who must be eliminated.

Ernie investigates the door and insists on a logical explanation, showing systematic inquiry, but this remains ordinary personal investigation rather than a materially developed scientific method driving understanding.
A nonordinary cosmic environment—a parallel/experimental dimension with its own government and visitors who pass between worlds—is central, and Ernie physically crosses into it.

Ernie triggers explosions that obliterate the entire experimental dimension into a blinding sun; the destruction of a whole (nascent) dimension is large-scale and causally central, though its scope is a small experimental realm, leaving materiality uncertain.

candidates.description: A government-sponsored experimental parallel dimension, coexisting spatially with Ernie's house, into which parallel-world scientists intend to seed a new civilization ('Adam and Eve') starting from the newlyweds' home. It is accessed via the appearing/disappearing extra door and a laundry chute, governs the plot's central mystery, and produces consequences including the wife's identity shifts, Ernie's duplication paradox, and the dimension's destruction.

novelty.rationale: The story posits coexisting dimensions occupying the same physical space with parallel versions of people, an experimental third realm sponsored by a parallel government to seed a new populated world. This is a totalizing departure from the empirical norm that reframes the entire domestic setting (impossibly larger hidden space, tilted floor, doubled wife) as a manufactured parallel reality.

cognitive_validation.rationale: Though comedic and satirical (garbled institutional names, budget politics), the phenomenon is given a coherent, immanent, nonsupernatural account: a government-funded scientific experiment with equipment that shifts dimensional equilibrium, 'transitional burnouts' to break molecular resistance, a reproducible field-force door entrance, and a systematic technical miscalculation producing the duplication paradox. The rules are internally consistent and drive the resolution rather than invoking magic.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The experimental dimension is the overriding narrative logic: the entire plot is Ernie investigating the anomalous door, being recruited into the experiment, confronting his duplicate, destroying the dimension, and escaping home. Every major event flows from and returns to this novum; it is not an incidental gadget.

estrangement.rationale: The reader-facing contrast is the ordinary newlywed house rendered uncanny: a door that appears and vanishes onto solid wall, a hidden space larger than its closet, a tilted floor, and a wife whose name and hair change. These estrange the domestic norm against the storyworld consequence that the home is the nucleus of a manufactured parallel dimension.

candidates.description: The extra hallway door that appears one night and vanishes the next, opening onto solid wall, considered as an isolated anomalous object.

novelty.rationale: A door that intermittently exists and opens onto solid wall is a clear departure from the empirical norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The door is later explained as a field-force entrance controlled by the experimenters' equipment, giving it a coherent immanent basis. Note: this candidate is best understood as a manifestation of the dimension novum rather than an independent novum.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: Taken in isolation the door is an entry device/symptom; the overriding narrative logic belongs to the experimental dimension it grants access to, not to the door as such. It does not independently determine the whole narrative.

estrangement.rationale: The vanishing door that opens onto solid wall estranges an everyday domestic fixture, driving Ernie's rational investigation, but functions as a gateway symptom of the larger dimensional novum.
